absent: Transmit completion reclamation policy and queue-full stop and wake behavior beyond the observed call sites.
Allocation and sizing and teardown of queue pairs and XDP program attachment and page pool lifecycle.
Small-packet zero-copy receive path and packet program handler internals.
Generic segmentation and checksum and flow-dissection helper internals owned elsewhere.
Device feature negotiation values and virtqueue notification transport details.
Rate-limited logging thresholds and device statistics layout.
Scatter-list and DMA mapping guarantees for premapped buffers.
Threading and NAPI polling context beyond the local transmit lock pairing shown.

findings.text: Bulk transmit service for upper packet layer accepts a device and a frame count and a frame collection and control flags, returning either a negative failure or the count actually queued. Success implies per-queue statistics were updated and the selected queue was released.

Transmission requires a loaded packet program observed through the receive queue pointer. Absence yields ENXIO without queue activity. Flag bits outside the defined transmit mask yield EINVAL. Doorbell activity occurs only when the flush request is present and preparation reports pending work, otherwise no kick is recorded.

Before queuing, the chosen send queue invokes an old-buffer release helper whose byte and packet totals are later folded into queue counters. After the loop, non-raw queues invoke a queue-full check helper. Final accounting adds reclaimed totals plus requested count and dropped remainder and kick indication between paired update begin and end markers.

Single-frame transmit requires headroom at least covering the device header length, otherwise an overflow failure is reported and the frame is left untouched. Fragmented frames expose their shared fragment count. On success the frame headroom and data start move backward by the header length and the new header area is cleared while checksum handling stays with upper layers. Linear and page fragments are described to the queue, and enqueue trouble is reported as no-space with release left to the caller.

Transmit queue choice derives from processor number cpu and counts curr_queue_pairs and nr_cpu_ids and xdp_queue_pairs. When pairs exceed processor count, selection uses a dedicated high range plus processor index under acquire and release pairing. Otherwise selection wraps processor number modulo pair count under transmit lock and unlock pairing. Get and put must bracket one transmit operation on the same queue.

Appending receive data coalesces into the current fragment when possible, releasing the incoming page through pool or generic path. Otherwise it attaches as a new fragment with computed offset. When the current socket buffer already holds the maximum fragment count, a fresh empty buffer is chained through frag list or next pointer and head accounting is extended. Length and true size updates apply to the head only when appending beyond the head.

Merged zero-copy receive dispatches on packet program verdict between paired RCU read markers. Pass builds a socket buffer from the first descriptor and attempts to attach followers. Success delivers the chain, while any construction or attach trouble discards followers and records a drop. Transmit and redirect verdicts produce no socket buffer and no drop record here. Other verdicts free the first descriptor and discard followers and record a drop.

Zero-copy receive subtracts header length from reported length and accounts bytes before descriptor conversion. Packets shorter than Ethernet header are counted as length errors and freed. Mergeable mode consults the buffer count converted from device endian. With an active program only single-buffer packets go to the program handler while multi-buffer packets take the abort path. Non-mergeable mode delegates to the small-packet path and mergeable mode to the merge path, and any resulting socket buffer proceeds to completion with preserved flags.

Follow-buffer collection expects an exact descriptor count. A missing descriptor stops the loop and counts a length error and abandons the remainder. Append path copies each follower into freshly allocated fragments and chains them. Allocation or conversion or chaining trouble discards all remaining followers and reports invalid argument, leaving the caller to free the head.

Receive completion conditionally reports hash only when device feature and capability agree, then validates checksum offload and tunnel header before delivery. Either validation failure logs a rate-limited warning and counts a frame error and frees the buffer. Valid packets get device assignment and fixed Ethernet network offset and recorded queue and protocol extraction and hand-off to generic receive.

Hash reporting maps transport-aware device reports to layer-four type and network-only reports to layer-three type and none or unknown values to no-hash type. The reported value combines low and high halves after little-endian conversion. Null header or socket buffer pointers cause silent return.

Tunnel header conversion delegates to base handling when no tunnel request is present. Tunnel requests require negotiated support and a single valid tunnel family and an inner segmentation kind other than plain datagram and a checksum request flag. Offsets must satisfy minimum header sizes and strict ordering from outer transport through inner network to inner transport. Validated packets gain inner protocol and tunnel segmentation markers with optional checksum variant and adjusted header offsets and an encapsulation mark.

Base header conversion maps wire segmentation kinds to generic segmentation types with transport lengths and minimum network sizes, rejecting unknown kinds and zero segment size. Checksum-requested packets must provide enough bytes for checksum coverage plus headers and must satisfy partial checksum setup and transport offset checks. Without checksum request, segmented packets undergo flow dissection with protocol matching and a retry for ambiguous datagram encapsulation. Transport-specific checks enforce correct checksum placement and segment count limits and rejection of fragment-based sizing. Undersized payloads are left unmarked.

Protocol helpers match or assign Ethernet protocol from wire segmentation kind, ignoring the congestion modifier and leaving already-set protocol untouched. The plain conversion wrapper forwards the header type to the base routine. Minimum network length helper selects between IPv4 and IPv6 header sizes.

Checksum offload handling treats non-tunnel packets with valid-data indication as already checked, promoting tunnel-checksum-marked packets to outer level only when negotiated. Tunnel segmentation requests reject valid-data indication as mutually exclusive with checksum request. Packets without relevant indications succeed without state change.

Zero-copy refill allocates up to the count of free descriptors. Empty allocation either arms a wakeup and returns success to deschedule polling when wakeup mode applies, or reports memory shortage otherwise. Each buffer reserves header space inside headroom and derives device address by backing off header length and enqueues a single premapped descriptor. Enqueue failure frees all not-yet-queued buffers and propagates the error while already-queued ones remain.
Premapped input-buffer insertion exposes queueing of a scatter table with caller data and context and allocation flags, delegating to the generic queue-add routine.

Wire packet header family shares fields flags and gso_type and gso_size and csum_start and csum_offset, with mergeable variant adding num_buffers and hash variant adding hash_report plus hash_value_lo and hash_value_hi, and tunnel variant adding inner_nh_offset and outer_th_offset. Completion path preserves flags across hash and checksum and tunnel processing before hand-off.

Device state links dev and vdev and queue pair counts curr_queue_pairs and xdp_queue_pairs and header length hdr_len and capability flags mergeable_rx_bufs and has_rss_hash_report and rx_tnl and rx_tnl_csum and queue arrays sq and rq. Send queues carry vq and sg and counters for bytes and packets and transmit totals and drops and kicks with an associated sync object. Receive queues carry vq and xdp_prog and napi and sg and zero-copy staging.
Transmit control uses architected mask XDP_XMIT_FLAGS_MASK for validation and bit XDP_XMIT_FLUSH to request doorbell notification.

Wire segmentation kinds include VIRTIO_NET_HDR_GSO_NONE and VIRTIO_NET_HDR_GSO_TCPV4 and VIRTIO_NET_HDR_GSO_TCPV6 and VIRTIO_NET_HDR_GSO_UDP and VIRTIO_NET_HDR_GSO_UDP_L4 and VIRTIO_NET_HDR_GSO_UDP_TUNNEL with VIRTIO_NET_HDR_GSO_UDP_TUNNEL_IPV6 variant and VIRTIO_NET_HDR_GSO_ECN modifier. Wire flag bits include VIRTIO_NET_HDR_F_NEEDS_CSUM and VIRTIO_NET_HDR_F_DATA_VALID and VIRTIO_NET_HDR_F_UDP_TUNNEL_CSUM. Generic counterparts include SKB_GSO_TCPV4 and SKB_GSO_TCPV6 and SKB_GSO_UDP and SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 and SKB_GSO_UDP_TUNNEL and SKB_GSO_UDP_TUNNEL_CSUM and SKB_GSO_DODGY and SKB_GSO_TCP_ECN.

Wire hash reports include VIRTIO_NET_HASH_REPORT_TCPv4 and VIRTIO_NET_HASH_REPORT_UDPv4 and VIRTIO_NET_HASH_REPORT_TCPv6 and VIRTIO_NET_HASH_REPORT_UDPv6 and VIRTIO_NET_HASH_REPORT_TCPv6_EX and VIRTIO_NET_HASH_REPORT_UDPv6_EX as transport types and VIRTIO_NET_HASH_REPORT_IPv4 and VIRTIO_NET_HASH_REPORT_IPv6 and VIRTIO_NET_HASH_REPORT_IPv6_EX as network types and VIRTIO_NET_HASH_REPORT_NONE for no hash.

Host-controlled lengths and offsets and segmentation kinds and checksum indications are untrusted. Short or inconsistent or unsupported values must be rejected before generic receive to avoid over-read or mis-delivery. Failure paths must free the in-progress buffer exactly once and account the appropriate length or frame error without double counting.

Zero-copy buffer lifecycle moves from refill allocation through device ownership to completion handling and finally to socket buffer construction or explicit free. Refill starvation pauses polling via wakeup arming. Completion either chains into a deliverable packet or releases all associated descriptors on error.
